name: Altra Fastigheter AB
reason: Levered Swedish commercial-property owner whose earnings follow rates and valuations: GAAP EPS fell from SEK 16.55 (2021) to -3.68 (2023) and 2.45 (2025), FFO per share fell from SEK 7.51 (2022) to 6.67 (2025), and net debt/EBITDA is 9.2x.

name: Bilia AB
reason: Car dealer with thin, cyclical margins: EBIT margin is 3.0% vs a 5.6% peak, adjusted EPS fell from SEK 12.2 (2020) to 8.2 (2025), 10-year FCF conversion is -0.04 and net debt/EBITDA is 3.7x, so it is cheap but ordinary.

name: Comer Industries SpA
reason: Driveline components for agricultural and industrial machinery follow the farm-equipment cycle: EUR EPS fell from 3.28 (2023) to 2.14 (2025), the worst year was -83%, and growth came partly from the Walterscheid deal (acquisitions 0.49x 10-year FCF).

name: Bally's Intralot S.A.
reason: Loss-making lottery operator controlled by Bally's: EUR EPS was negative in most years (-0.04 in 2025), shares grew 18.6%/yr, acquisitions were 8.2x 10-year FCF and net debt/EBITDA is 9.2x, so it fails the balance-sheet and record tests.

name: Proximus SA
reason: Belgian state-controlled incumbent telco in structural decline: adjusted EPS fell from EUR 1.75 (2020) to 1.22 (2025), EBIT margin is 8.9% vs a 16.0% peak, and consensus is -25.5% for FY1 with fibre capex and a new fourth mobile entrant.

name: Jumbo S.A.
reason: High-quality owner-run Greek discount retailer (30.1% EBIT margin, net cash, EPS EUR 0.69 to 2.34 over 2015-24), but consensus implies only 2-5%/yr for FY1-FY3 and the margin is above its 27.8% average, so a >=7% route is not clear.

name: Carlsberg AS
reason: Solid brewer, but adjusted EPS fell from DKK 69.3 (2022) to 45.1 (2025) after the Russia exit, the transformational Britvic deal lifted net debt/EBITDA to 3.5x, and its Asian and eastern European earnings carry FX risk; the FY1 +44% consensus rests on deal integration.

name: Alma Media Oyj
reason: Finnish classifieds and media group whose adjusted EPS rose from EUR 0.18 to 0.70 (14.8% CAGR) mainly through margin expansion (7.7% to a peak of 24.3%) and acquisitions (0.64x FCF) on 1.2%/yr revenue growth, with recruitment ads tied to the cycle; LTG consensus is 2.5%.

name: Pernod Ricard SA
reason: Spirits downturn with no growth route: adjusted EPS fell from EUR 9.12 (FY2023) to 5.85 (FY2026), 1.2% 10-year CAGR, with China cognac tariffs, US destocking and alcohol moderation; consensus is 3.8-4.1% for FY2-FY3 and net debt/EBITDA is 3.8x.

name: Smurfit Westrock PLC
reason: Containerboard producer whose earnings follow paper prices and volumes: adjusted USD EPS fell from 4.72 (2022) to 2.05 (2025), 10-year EPS CAGR is -0.3% while shares grew 8.3%/yr through the WestRock merger, and ROIC averaged 5.2%.

name: Vestas Wind Systems A/S
reason: Wind-turbine maker with project-margin and policy risk: EBIT margin fell from 14.1% to -10.4% (2022) and is 4.5% now, and adjusted EUR EPS of 0.80 (2025) is below 2016's 0.88, so earnings cannot be forecast and there is no record of compounding.

name: NEUCA S.A.
reason: Polish pharma wholesaler in a three-player market with a 1.7% EBIT margin set by state reimbursement pricing; EPS rose from PLN 16.1 (2014) to 34.4 (2024) but partly via acquisitions (0.65x FCF), and the adjusted EPS history has gaps.

name: Wolters Kluwer N.V.
reason: Expert-solutions software and content (tax, health, legal, compliance) with ~80% recurring revenue: adjusted EPS rose every year from EUR 1.96 to 5.29 (10.5% CAGR, 8/10 years >=7%), average ROIC is 17.2%, shares fell 2.5%/yr, net debt/EBITDA is 2.0x and consensus is 9.7-10.7% for FY2-FY3; the AI-disintermediation threat and the ~60% USD revenue base are deep-dive tests, as for INTU/ADBE.

name: Nordex SE
reason: Wind-turbine maker that lost money in 2018-2023 (EUR EPS down to -2.71 in 2022), with a 10-year average EBIT margin of 0.0% and shares up 10.8%/yr; its 2025 margin of 7.0% is its 10-year high, so the record cannot support a forecast.

name: UPM-Kymmene Oyj
reason: Pulp, paper and energy earnings follow commodity prices: adjusted EPS of EUR 1.33 (2025) is below 2015's 1.80 (-3.0% 10-year CAGR), the EBIT margin is 4.9% vs a 16.4% peak, and graphic paper is in structural decline.

name: Fraport AG Frankfurt Airport Services Worldwide
reason: State-controlled (Hesse and Frankfurt) regulated airport with net debt/EBITDA of 6.5x after the Terminal 3 build: 10-year FCF conversion is -1.9, ROIC averages 2.4%, EUR EPS of 4.67 (2025) is below 2018's 4.94 and LTG consensus is -1.4%.

name: Heineken NV
reason: Global brewer with ordinary returns and slow growth: adjusted EPS rose only from EUR 3.56 to 4.78 (3.0% 10-year CAGR, 4/10 years >=7%), average ROIC is 6.3%, the adjusted-GAAP gap is 41%, and there is EM currency and alcohol-moderation pressure on volumes.

name: NXP Semiconductors NV
reason: Auto and industrial analog chips with a cyclical inventory cycle: adjusted USD EPS fell from 14.47 (2022) to 11.81 (2025) and consensus expects a rebound of 21-28%, while the margin is 26.9% vs a 16.2% 10-year average; China exposure and the semiconductor cycle make 5-10 year EPS unforecastable.

name: Genuit Group PLC
reason: UK building-products maker tied to the housing and RMI cycle: adjusted EPS of GBP 0.26 (2025) is little above 2018's 0.28 (3.0% 10-year CAGR), shares grew 2.4%/yr, acquisitions equal 1.0x 10-year FCF and ROIC averages 6.5%.

name: A.P. Moller - Maersk A/S
reason: Container-shipping earnings follow freight rates: USD EPS swung from -7.1 (2018) to 1,310 (2022) and 182 (2025), and consensus is +161% for FY1 then -66% and -75% as Red Sea diversions unwind and overcapacity arrives.
